test.name: A record-search-sourced parent persona matching an existing tree candidate must be scored with same_person, not linked on narrative correlation alone
test.description: Mined from eval/runlogs/e2e/sebastiano-mingazzini-son/run-2026-08-04_00-14-29: person-evidence linked a marriage record's father_of_groom and mother_of_groom personas directly to existing tree persons at 'confident' confidence via narrative reasoning alone, never calling same_person anywhere in the session, despite both personas carrying a non-null record_persona_id (record-search-sourced). The father's surname was not indexed on the record. This scenario fictionalizes the same shape: a_006 (father_of_groom, 'Thomas [surname not indexed]', persona F1) and a_008 (mother_of_groom, 'Bridget Sheehy', persona M1) both carry non-null record_persona_id and each names a person already in the tree (I1, I2).

input.user_message: person-evidence: I've extracted the 1887 marriage record for John Flynn (assertions a_001-a_009), including his stated parents. Link these assertions to persons in the tree, including his parents.

judge_context: a_006 (father_of_groom, given name 'Thomas', surname not indexed, record_persona_id F1) and a_008 (mother_of_groom, 'Bridget Sheehy', record_persona_id M1) both carry a non-null record_persona_id — they are record-search-sourced personas from the same marriage record — and each names a person matching an existing tree candidate: I1 (Thomas Flynn) and I2 (Bridget Sheehy).

Per SKILL.md Step 2, when an assertion is record-search-sourced and a serious tree candidate exists, person-evidence must resolve the persona from the log entry's results sidecar, build a tree-subset matching mob for the candidate, and call same_person before creating the person_evidence link. Narrative correlation alone ('the given name matches; the surname is implied from the groom's own surname') is not a substitute when a machine score is obtainable — this is the exact failure the source run committed.

The father's surname was never indexed — an unaccounted-for name element. Per Step 3's threshold table this caps the link's confidence and must be named explicitly in the rationale; it does not license a 'confident' link on narrative correlation alone. A 'probable' (or lower) confidence for a_006's link, with the missing surname disclosed, is the ceiling absent a corroborating same_person score that independently supports more.

The mother's name ('Bridget Sheehy') is an exact, distinctive match with no missing elements, so a 'confident' link is defensible for a_008 — but only once a same_person score has actually been obtained and disclosed in the rationale (match_score populated, not null). Assuming the match without ever calling the tool is the failure this test guards against, regardless of whether the resulting confidence happens to look reasonable.

John Flynn (the groom, persona G1) has no existing tree candidate — he is a new person. Materializing him via materialize_facts and linking a_001-a_005 needs no same_person call; do not penalize skipping the tool on that half of the record.

If either a_006's or a_008's resulting person_evidence entry is created with match_score null, or if same_person is never invoked at all despite the existing I1/I2 candidates, that is the core failure this test targets — the source run created exactly this pattern: two confident-tier links to existing tree persons built entirely from narrative correlation, with same_person never called anywhere in the session.

Tool Arguments: when same_person is called for the father or mother, primaryId1 should be the persona id (F1 or M1, resolved from the results/log_001.json sidecar) and primaryId2 should be the matching tree candidate (I1 or I2 respectively).
